candidate.name: intraday_range_local_peak_clock_dispersion_236p
candidate.mechanism: Within-half clock dispersion of strict local maxima in the minute high-low log-range sequence, using only peak positions after the topology is identified.
candidate.formula: For each half set q_i=ln(high_i/low_i), identify strict interior peaks q_i>q_i-1 and q_i>q_i+1 for i=1..118, map x_i=i/119, require at least two peaks, compute population Var(x) in each half, and average the two variances.
candidate.fixed_support: Exactly 236 interior local-peak opportunities from the fixed 240 standard bars; exclude 09:30, endpoints, and every cross-lunch, cross-date, or cross-stock comparison.
candidate.zero_and_missing_semantics: Exact-zero ranges and tied neighbors remain valid nonpeaks. Require all 240 high/low pairs finite, positive, and ordered plus at least two strict peaks per half. Never drop an opportunity, add jitter, break ties, fill, clip, threshold, or substitute.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_clock_center_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both locate high-low range activity on the intraday clock.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor is the range-mass-weighted first clock moment across all 240 bars. Campaign094 discards every magnitude after strict local maxima are identified and averages the second central moment of unweighted peak positions separately inside each half. Moving nonpeak range mass changes the clock center but leaves Campaign094 unchanged when peak topology is preserved.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_amount_local_peak_density_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor counts amount peaks on adjacent amount triples. Campaign094 reads no amount, does not use peak count as the score, and measures the clock dispersion of range peaks with a two-per-half support rule.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_weak_order_entropy_236t and intraday_range_weak_order_time_reversal_divergence_236t
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: All depend on the ordinal topology of three-bar range neighborhoods.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those factors tabulate the full weak-order pattern distribution or its reversal divergence across every interior triple. Campaign094 retains only strict center-maximum events and measures where they occur on the half-session clock; permuting identical local patterns across clock positions can change Campaign094 while leaving pattern frequencies unchanged.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_intrabar_range_participation_entropy_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both characterize dispersion of intraday range activity.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Participation entropy uses normalized range magnitudes over all bars and is invariant to their clock permutation. Campaign094 is magnitude-free after peak detection and changes when peak clocks cluster or spread despite the same range-mass distribution.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_morning_afternoon_range_profile_similarity_120b
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both keep morning and afternoon range structures separate.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor compares the two complete range profiles for similarity. Campaign094 never compares morning with afternoon; it computes peak-clock variance inside each half and then averages the two scalars.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_extreme_arrival_order_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor times global price high/low arrivals. Campaign094 ignores price levels and global extremes and instead uses every strict local maximum of bar range inside each half.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_amount_peak_timing_alignment_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both reference timing of range peaks.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor compares the single range-magnitude peak clock with the single amount peak clock. Campaign094 reads no amount and summarizes the dispersion of all strict local range-peak clocks, regardless of which peak has maximum magnitude.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_close_transition_range_quadratic_efficiency_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both read high-low ranges on the same fixed minute grid.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Campaign093 pools squared range magnitudes against squared adjacent close transitions and reads close. Campaign094 reads no close, performs no magnitude allocation, and depends only on local range-peak positions.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: candidate49_intraday_cumulative_vwap_crossing_rate_240m_v1
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both use the completed standard-minute grid.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Candidate49 counts causal close-versus-cumulative-VWAP crossings and requires amount/volume. Campaign094 uses high/low range topology only and never touches the prospective ledgers.
